message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of water is **about –2.2 °C**.

**Why?**  
The phase diagram of water shows that the ice–water equilibrium line (the melting curve) slopes downward as pressure decreases. At the triple point (≈ 0.61 kPa) the melting point is 0 °C. As you move to higher pressures the melting point rises toward 0 °C at 1 atm. Conversely, at lower pressures the melting point drops. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is roughly –2.2 °C, which is the temperature at which ice and liquid water coexist in equilibrium.
